planting.note: Plant this female Michigan State University selection on a sturdy trellis in full sun; it needs a male arguta vine nearby for pollination.

directions: MSU is a female hardy kiwi vine discovered growing at Michigan State University, selected for its large, oval-shaped fruit and vigorous vine habit. Like all Actinidia arguta, it is dioecious and bears no fruit without a male pollinator planted within range, with one male generally able to pollinate six to eight females. Train the vine on a sturdy permanent trellis in full sun and well-drained soil, and prune hard each winter to control its vigorous growth and keep fruiting wood accessible. It tolerates heat and humidity well but dislikes wet feet, so avoid poorly drained sites.

planting.note: Plant this female vine on a sturdy arbor in full sun with a male arguta pollinator nearby; it is prized for mild, non-bitter skin.

directions: Cordifolia is a female hardy kiwi selection noted for high sweetness and round-shouldered fruit with non-bitter skin, letting the smooth, grape-sized berries be eaten out of hand without the astringency some arguta selections show near the stem end. As a dioecious vine it must be paired with a male hardy kiwi for pollination. Grow on a strong permanent support in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, and thin side shoots in winter to keep the fruiting canopy open and manageable.

planting.note: Plant this male-only USDA selection within range of several female arguta cultivars; it bears no fruit itself but supplies pollen for the whole planting.

directions: Fairchild, also sold under its USDA selection number 74-52, is a male hardy kiwi grown solely as a pollen source and listed as effective at pollinating a wide range of Actinidia arguta female cultivars. Since the species is dioecious, female vines set little or no fruit without a nearby male in bloom at the same time. Plant it centrally among the female vines on a shared trellis system, and prune it hard after bloom since no fruit production is expected from this selection.

planting.note: Plant this US National Arboretum female selection on a sturdy trellis with a male arguta pollinator nearby.

directions: Arbor-Eat-Um, also catalogued under its selection number NA-7, is a female hardy kiwi that originated from the U.S. National Arboretum's kiwiberry collection. Like other arguta females it is dioecious and requires a male vine blooming nearby for pollination and fruit set. Provide a heavy-duty trellis or pergola, since mature vines become quite woody and productive plantings carry substantial fruit weight. Full sun and well-drained, fertile soil give the best fruit quality, and winter pruning of the previous year's growth keeps the canopy manageable for harvest.

planting.note: Plant this early-ripening female vine where its two-to-three-week head start on Ken's Red extends the hardy kiwi harvest window.

directions: Fifty-Five is a female hardy kiwi selection valued chiefly for ripening earlier than almost any other arguta cultivar, reportedly two to three weeks ahead of the widely planted Ken's Red. That early ripening window can help a home orchard spread harvest over more of the fall rather than having the whole hardy kiwi crop come in at once. It still needs a male arguta vine nearby for pollination, since the species is dioecious, and performs best on a sturdy trellis in full sun with annual winter pruning to control vigorous growth.

planting.note: Plant this numbered selection from Cornell's Geneva, New York hardy kiwi breeding collection alongside a male arguta vine on a sturdy trellis.

directions: Geneva 3 is a numbered selection from the same Cornell Geneva, New York hardy kiwi breeding and evaluation collection that produced the better-known plain Geneva cultivar, offered as a distinct clone within that program. It shares the family's good cold hardiness and reliable production on a well-sited trellis. Being dioecious, it needs a male Actinidia arguta vine planted within pollinating range to set fruit, and benefits from full sun, well-drained fertile soil, and annual winter pruning to keep the vigorous vine's fruiting wood within reach.

planting.note: Plant dormant bushes in fall or early spring in fertile soil with afternoon shade in hot climates; self-fertile and mildew-resistant.

directions: Red Cherry is a currant cultivar grown for short, loose clusters of unusually large, bright dark red berries with a tart, acidic flavor. The upright, vigorous bush is self-fertile, sets heavy crops without a second plant, and shows good resistance to mildew, which makes it a reasonable pick for humid gardens where currants often struggle. It tolerates light shade well, so it can be tucked along the north side of a building or under high shade where little else fruits, though some sun improves yield. Give it fertile, evenly moist soil and mulch to keep roots cool through summer heat.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade when young; pair with a second cultivar for cross-pollination.

directions: Pennsylvania Golden is a One Green World pawpaw selection noted for good crops of large fruit with the rich banana-mango-melon flavor and custard texture pawpaw fans prize. Like all pawpaws it is self-incompatible, so plant a second, genetically distinct cultivar within about 50 feet for reliable pollination, and give young trees partial shade and consistently moist, humus-rich soil before transitioning them to more sun as they mature. The tree's large, drooping, tropical-looking leaves are also a strong ornamental asset in a shaded border.

planting.note: Plant this female cultivar in full sun on lean, well-drained soil with a male sea berry planted within range for pollination.

directions: Mary is a female sea buckthorn (seaberry) cultivar offered alongside the better-known Askola and Leikora selections, grown for the tart, vitamin-dense orange fruit typical of the species. Its nitrogen-fixing roots tolerate poor, sandy, or coastal soils that would stunt most fruiting shrubs, but the plant dislikes waterlogged ground and performs poorly in heavy, wet clay. Being dioecious, Mary needs a male sea berry growing within roughly 50 to 100 feet to set any fruit at all, and the thorny canopy benefits from an annual thinning cut to keep clustered fruit within reach for hand harvest.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in full sun on well-drained soil; self-fertile, drought-tolerant once established like other jujube cultivars.

directions: Empress Gee is a named jujube cultivar sold alongside long-established selections such as Li, Lang, and Honey Jar, bearing the sweet, apple-crisp fruit that gives jujube its Chinese Date nickname. Like other jujubes, it is heat-loving, extremely drought-tolerant once established, and largely self-fertile, though a second cultivar nearby can improve fruit set. Plant it in full sun on well-drained soil, since jujube roots rot readily in heavy, poorly drained ground, and expect the deciduous tree to sucker somewhat from the roots, which can be managed by mowing or removing shoots as they appear.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in full sun on well-drained soil; self-fertile, drought-tolerant once established like other jujube cultivars.

directions: Xian Beauty is a named jujube cultivar offered alongside classics such as Chico, GA-866, and Shanxi Li, producing the crisp, sweet, apple-like fruit typical of Ziziphus jujuba once it colors up in late summer and fall. The tree is heat-loving and drought-tolerant once established, shrugging off the kind of baking summer sun that stresses most temperate fruit trees, and is largely self-fertile, though planting a second cultivar nearby tends to improve yields. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, since standing water quickly damages the root system, and expect some root suckering that can be mowed off or left to form a thicket if a hedge effect is wanted.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in full sun to partial shade; a Ukrainian-bred selection valued for unusually large, sweet fruit and cold hardiness to zone 4.

directions: Coral Blaze is one of a group of Ukrainian cornelian cherry selections marketed alongside Pioneer, Red Dawn, and Sunrise, bred for unusually large, sweet, flavorful fruit compared to seedling Cornus mas and for reliable cold hardiness to USDA zone 4. Like other cornelian cherry cultivars, it produces clouds of tiny yellow flowers on bare branches in very early spring, among the first bloom of the year, followed later by tart-to-sweet red drupes once fully ripe. Give it full sun to light shade and well-drained soil; the small tree tolerates a wide range of conditions and needs little care once established, though fruit quality improves with a second cornelian cherry cultivar planted nearby for cross-pollination.
